title: Rock Me Maharaji: The Little Guru Without a Prayer (Rolling Stone, March 14, 1974)
author: Richard Levine, reporting accounts by premies and ex-premies (Bob Hallowitz, 'Alan')
edition_cited: Rolling Stone no. 156, March 14, 1974, pp. 36-50, as reproduced at ex-premie.org/pages/rollings_article.htm
locator_hints: Section after the Astrodome press session with Mahatma Ashokanand: the initiation as described by disillusioned ex-premies (dark room of up to 25, mahatma 'presses his knuckles forcefully against each person's eyeballs')
Washington D.C. ashram section: Bob Hallowitz, neurophysiologist, on the experience after a month of meditation ('an intense white light that filled his head') and his pineal theory
Background section: 'Alan' on his hand dissolving while meditating and on nothing happening when he tried to force it
summary: Long 1974 magazine report on the Houston 'Millennium' festival. Two passages matter here. First, the initiation as ex-members described it to the reporter: up to twenty-five people in a darkened room for hours, then a demonstration lasting minutes in which the mahatma presses his knuckles hard on each initiate's closed eyes, producing flashes that the writer attributes to pressure on the optic nerve. Second, a practising premie, the neurophysiologist Bob Hallowitz, says that after a month of daily meditation, at the climax of a recurring nightmare, an intense white light filled his head together with bell sounds, fragrance and vibration: an event not tied to pressing at that moment. Another premie reports perceptual changes while meditating (his hand seeming to dissolve) and says that trying to force a trance produced little.
why_relevant: Sets a pressure-induced first light beside a later, apparently stimulus-free light reported by the same movement's practitioner; both dated 1974 and attributed.

date_evidence.basis: Issue number, date and pages as printed on the reproduction page (Rolling Stone, Issue No. 156, March 14, 1974, pp. 36-50); the magazine itself was not seen, and the web page carries no posting date.

author_basis: Bylined journalist (Richard Levine) in Rolling Stone; interviewees named in the article
notes: Safety: eye pressure (forceful, applied by another person). Reader extract; the last 1,986 characters of the page were not read. The initiation description is second-hand (reporter relaying ex-premies); Hallowitz's account is first-person as quoted by the reporter. The Hallowitz light occurred in a dream/nightmare context: the reading agent should weigh whether it counts as practice-linked.
